To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) de novo sequencing is a useful method for the analysis of MS/MS spectra; (ii) it is a useful complement to database search engines; and (iii) it can be used to determine the accuracy of search engine results, particularly when the search engine is not able to assign the spectrum.

(1) peptide fragmentation is a complex process; (2) there are many known fragmentation rules, which are not used by current search engines; (3) the rules of peptide fragmentation are well documented; (4) the most important rule is that peptide fragmentation is not random; (5) the fragmentation process can be predicted; (6) the rules of fragmentation can be applied to determine peptide sequences; (7) the rules are useful for data validation and for the identification of false positives;

the most important factors in de novo peptide sequence determination by CID are the following: 1) the presence of a single, dominant y-type ion, 2) the absence of b ions, and 3) the presence of y ions with a mass difference of 1 Da between successive ions.
